cluster.members: each field that states a resolution
cluster.source: the clock of the cluster component that wrote the value

read.source: the wall clock of the host that ran the collector

doesNotEstablish: That a caller obtained a completion at any instant. A Ready endpoint, a Ready pod, a replica count, a sync state, and a health state are what the cluster and the delivery controller published. None of them is a request that a caller sent and had answered.
That a field with a state other than reported had any value. A field that was not reported is not zero, not Ready, not synced, and not healthy.
The state of the cluster at a sample whose read is not answered. A read that did not answer is not an empty namespace.
The instant of a change. A change is bounded by two reads, and the interval between them is the smallest interval that a stream supports.
That a request reached a Ready endpoint, or that a pod behind a Ready endpoint could serve inference.
That the delivery controller applied the commit it reported, or that an object of the release was rendered at that commit.
The cause of a change. A stream holds no event, no log, and no message.
A result of an experiment. A stream is evidence that an analysis reads. This module computes no metric and gives no verdict.
limitations: The instants read.startedAt and read.finishedAt are the wall clock of the host that ran the collector, in UTC, to one millisecond. A wall clock can be set while a collection runs. The end line names each reading whose start is before the finish of the reading before it.

A reading is the state at an instant that is not known. The instant is not before read.startedAt and not after read.finishedAt, when the API server answered from its present state. The workload read is one command that makes one request for each kind, so its kinds are not one atomic reading.
The timeout of a read is the timeout of each request that kubectl makes. A read makes more than one request, so it can take longer than the timeout and still answer.

An instant that a cluster component wrote is on the clock of that component. It is normalised to UTC and keeps its resolution, which is one second for each instant that Kubernetes writes into the fields read here. It is not on the clock of the collecting host.

The difference between the clock of the collecting host and a clock of the cluster was not measured. The end line counts the cluster instants, other than a deletion timestamp, that are later than the finish of the read that returned them. A count above zero shows that the two clocks differ. A count of zero does not bound the difference.
The deletion timestamp of a pod is the instant at which its grace period ends. It is not the instant of the request to delete the pod, and it can be later than the read that returned it.
No order between two events is established when the events are less than one second apart and one of them is a cluster instant, or when both are in the interval of one read.
A state that began and ended between two readings is in no reading.

The Kubernetes API omits a status count of a Deployment that is zero, and it omits a count that the controller did not write yet. A reading states each omitted count as missing. It does not state zero.
An identity is a name and a UID. It is valid for the life of that object on that cluster. It is not a stable identity of a replica.
A pod that left the read and a pod that entered it are two facts. No reading states that one pod replaced another.
The revision of a pod is the revision annotation of the ReplicaSet that owns it, in the same read. It is missing when that ReplicaSet is not in the read.
A reading with more than 64 pods of the two tiers states no pod.
The restart counts of a pod are two sums: one over its containers and one over its init containers. A restart of an ephemeral container is not read.

The collection names the commit of the working tree that ran the collector, and the SHA-256 of the collector script and of its library. It does not state whether the tree had a change that was not committed.
omitted: The addresses of an endpoint and of a pod.
The node name, the zone, and the hostname of an endpoint and of a pod.
The images, the commands, the environment variables, and the volumes of a pod.
Each message of a condition, of a container state, and of an operation.
The repository address of the Application.
The name of the kubeconfig context. A context name can hold an account identifier.
Every pod of the namespace that is not a pod of one of the two tiers. A reading states their number and nothing else.
